name: Avenue Supermarts Ltd. (DMart)
business_summary: India's largest listed value-retail supermarket chain (DMart) with mostly owned stores, EDLP pricing and a focus on foods, FMCG and general merchandise/apparel; also DMart Ready e-commerce. TTM sales Rs 74,223 cr (+16%), EBITDA margin ~7.5%, PAT Rs 3,116 cr, promoter holding 74.5% (Damani family). Growth is driven by ~20% annual area growth and mid-single-digit LFL; it is valued at ~71x trailing earnings so the stock is highly sensitive to growth/margin delivery and the discount rate.

revenue_mix.geography: India; West & South heavy (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Karnataka)

cost_structure.input: Purchase of stock-in-trade / COGS (food, FMCG, GM, apparel)

exposures.mechanism: Revenue +16-18% y/y is ~60% store-area growth, ~40% LFL/ticket. +5pp urban demand growth -> LFL +2.5pp -> revenue +2.5%; fixed-cost (rent/staff ~50% of opex) leverage gives ~1.5x flow-through: EBITDA +4-5% at 7.5% margin. EV/MCap ~1.02, persistence 0.5 -> ~+2.3 from earnings alone; adds ~+1.7 for growth-multiple support (P/E 71.5, price already -22% in 6m on growth/margin worry). Net ~+4.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5
BusinessLine: store network +20% but sales/sq ft +0.6%; CNBC TV18/Moneycontrol 12 Oct: margin miss, stock -3-4%; Business Standard 16 Oct: 3-yr low, -28% from April high

exposures.mechanism: Broad GST cut on staples/FMCG/apparel lowers shelf prices, lifts volumes and trade-down traffic for the value format (DMart is >50% FMCG+food; apparel/GM ~ 30-35%). +3pp effective price cut x elasticity ~0.7 -> volume +2%, revenue neutral-to-positive; gross margin neutral (EDLP, pass-through). ~+3 incl. sentiment; one-off (persistence 0.3). Model knowledge on GST 2.0 (Sep 2025); confirm current rates.

Quick-commerce (Blinkit, Instamart, Zepto, BB Now) is eroding top-up grocery baskets in top-8 cities where DMart has dense stores; DMart Ready scales slowly. If 3% of DMart food/FMCG GMV (~55% of sales -> 1.7% of sales) is lost with ~40% decremental margin -> EBITDA -9%; partly offset by catchment of tier-2/3 where q-comm absent -> -3 net. Structural (persistence 1.0) but contested; analyst commentary after Q2 flagged slowing sales/sq ft (+0.6%).

evidence.note: BusinessLine: store network +20% but sales/sq ft +0.6%; CNBC TV18/Moneycontrol 12 Oct: margin miss, stock -3-4%; Business Standard 16 Oct: 3-yr low, -28% from April high

exposures.mechanism: Shift of grocery share from kirana to organised value retail: DMart is the largest listed beneficiary (revenue 74k cr TTM, +16% vs nominal food retail ~+9%). +1 unit ~ +1pp/yr faster organised share gain -> revenue +1.5% p.a. compounding; valuation (71x) capitalises long runway so w ~+2.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: Stock P/E 71.5, duration ~30y of cash flows: +25bp discount-rate shift = ~-2% equity via Gordon-style sensitivity (1/(r-g) with r-g~4%: 0.25/4 = -6%, damped 0.35 for the portion of the multiple driven by rates rather than growth). Empirical US 10y beta -0.5 (t -0.8) consistent in sign.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: Borrowings are rising (interest 64 cr in Q2 vs 35 cr a year ago; Fortune India 12 Oct flagged rising debt) but still ~2% of sales; +25bp on ~2,500 cr floating debt = ~6 cr/yr vs PAT ~3,100 cr = -0.2%. Mostly captured by F_GSEC_10Y_IN discount-rate edge; kept small to avoid double counting.

evidence.note: Fortune India: brokerages flag rising debt
Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: +2pp food inflation raises nominal ticket size (food ~ 50% of sales: revenue +1%), but DMart's EDLP pricing absorbs part of input inflation (gross margin ~14-15% compresses 10-20bp if it lags) and demand elasticity trims volumes. Net ~+0.8 with wide range. Pack shows edible oil +1.99 (t 1.6) and wheat +1.26 (t 1.5): same positive sign, not significant, so weight shrunk.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: Diesel/freight ~2.5% of sales. +10% Brent -> diesel ~+5% (retail prices regulated, pass-through partial) -> logistics +0.13% of sales vs 7.5% EBITDA margin = EBITDA -1.7%; EV/MCap 1.02; persistence 0.3 -> -0.5; adds consumer wallet squeeze via CPI -> -0.8. Pack Brent coefficient not in top-12 (insignificant).

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: Employee cost ~3.5-4% of sales (largely contract/outsourced staff). +2pp wage growth -> +0.07-0.08% of sales -> EBITDA -1.0%; EV/MCap 1.02; persistence 0.5 -> -0.5; offset +0.1 by higher disposable income -> -0.4.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: Implementation of the four labour codes raises statutory wage-base/gratuity and contract-labour compliance cost. Staff ~4% of sales; +5% effective cost -> 0.2% of sales -> EBITDA -2.7%; persistence 1.0 but gradual, ~50% passed via EDLP efficiencies -> -0.6. Model knowledge on codes (notified Nov 2025); implementation timing uncertain.
FIIs hold 8.5% (down from 9.2% in Jun-26) and DMart is a classic FPI-favoured quality-growth name; +$5bn/qtr inflows lift high-multiple compounders ~ +2-3% relative (beta to FPI-driven rerating).

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 sales 19,644 cr, OP 1,393 cr (OPM 7%), PAT 743 cr; mcap 2,22,894 cr, P/E 71.5

exposures.mechanism: Store capex (~4,000-5,000 cr/yr, owns most stores) has steel ~8-10% of build cost: +7% steel -> capex +0.6% -> ROCE -2bp. Immaterial. Pack shows iron ore -3.21 (t -2.0): statistically notable but likely a proxy for risk-on/commodity-cycle vs defensive-growth rotation, not a fundamental link; weight not raised.

exposures.mechanism: Imported content (edible oils/pulses sourcing, some GM/electronics, ~10% of purchases is import-linked) so +3% USD/INR -> COGS +0.3% -> margin pressure partly passed on; also hurts FII-sentiment. EBITDA -1.5% x 0.3 persistence -> -0.5; plus FPI sentiment -0.1.

current_state.trend: Revenue growth steady at ~17-18% on ~20% area growth but sales per sq ft +0.6% (BusinessLine 16 Oct); earnings growth lags revenue; leverage rising; stock at 3-year low, -22% in 6m, -28% from April-2026 high (Business Standard 16 Oct).
current_state.valuation: Stock P/E 71.5 (TTM EPS 47.8), P/B 8.5, ROE 12.9%, ROCE 17.2%; screener flags low 3y ROE 13.5%; no dividend. Historic P/E range materially higher (>100x in 2021-24, model knowledge), so de-rating is under way.
